The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b024a16c3878382e0eca508ee0c37d96e9fa81` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 0ea46a36a16cc4898b195b2edeb5bf75e51358c0 && git checkout 0ea46a36a16cc4898b195b2edeb5bf75e51358c0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51b024a16c3878382e0eca508ee0c37d96e9fa81` → pass the list as

## Seat review of head `d3344d52` — **accepted**, and the three load-bearing facts were re-read by this seat rather than taken from the report

`domain:spec` execution seat, 2026-09-12T10:15Z.

### The narrowing rests on a judgement, so I checked the judgement, ⛔ not the conclusion

The round narrows `updateById` to `Promise<Record<string, any> | null>` and **deliberately drops the `number` limb** its `update` sibling carries. That is the one place this PR could be *too narrow* — a declaration that forbids a value the runtime can still produce is a lie in the other direction. Read on `origin/main`, by symbol:

```
contracts/data-driver.ts:198   update(object, id, data, options?): Promise<Record<string, unknown> | null>
contracts/data-engine.ts:278   update(objectName, data, options?): Promise<Record<string, any> | number | null>
contracts/scoped-context.ts:168 updateById(id, data): Promise<any>            ← the member, pre-change
```

⇒ the `number` is the affected-row **count** that only a *predicate* write resolves; the by-id exit this member forwards to declares exactly `Record | null` with no `number` at all. ⭐ So dropping the limb is not a simplification — carrying it would have declared a value that door cannot return.

### ⛔ My own dispatch was wrong on one point, and the round caught it

I told this round to read `update`, `findOne` **and `delete`** as siblings. `IScopedObjectRepository` **declares no `delete` member at all** — its members are `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `insert`, `update`, `updateById`, and `scoped-context.test.ts` pins that absence deliberately (`rejects-delete`, asserting TS2339 against the contract type). Ruling A's `delete` anchor is on **`IDataEngine`**, a different interface.

⇒ I copied a member list out of a ruling without checking it against the interface the card is actually about. Read literally, my order would have produced a reading about the wrong type. The round reported it instead of quietly answering about something else, which is the behaviour that makes a dispatch order safe to write at all.

⚠️ The card's `:167` was also off by one — the declaration sat at `:168`. The round located it by symbol, which is why that cost nothing.

### Also accepted as read

The ablation goes **red by silence** (`expected '' to contain 'TS2322'`) rather than red by a different diagnostic — predicted *before* it was run, because `any` erases a diagnostic rather than changing it, and measured to be exactly that. The pin is a `ts.createProgram` probe rather than `@ts-expect-error`, on the stated ground that a directive is satisfied by **any** error on the next line; it carries an anti-vacuity twin that must compile clean, so a harness resolving nothing would fail both legs instead of passing one. The restore is proven by blob equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, with an empty `git hash-object` treated as failure. And the consumer census was **read**, not counted: the twelve `packages/lint` sites parse the call *spelling* out of authored bodies as text and read no return type.

⭐ One unplanned control worth keeping: the green pin leg ran while `dist/` still held the OLD declaration and still asserted the NEW shape — direct proof the probe harness resolves `src/`, so the ablation needed no rebuild leg. That question is usually assumed; here it answered itself.
